newsitem.title: USA: Berkshire Realty says sees retail dilutive.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire Realty says sees retail dilutive.

text.p: Berkshire Realty Co Inc said Monday it sees its 1996 acquisitions performing at expected levels later this year, and it expects retail sales to date will be about $0.02 per share dilutive to funds from operations (FFO) in 1997.

The company also said it became self-managed in March of this year, which will improve its profitability for 1997. The company said its retail divestiture strategy will improve its future earnings growth.

The company said it expected minimal FFO growth in the first quarter of 1997 for two reasons. There was a softening in occupancies in some of its Atlanta, Greenville and Charlotte assets, although it expects to improve upon occupancies in Atlanta and Greenville.
Also, the company said its retail portfolio posted lower earnings due to the decision to restructure the tenant base at one of the shopping centers to position it for future sale.
The company reported earnings per share for the first quarter of $0.15 compared to $0.01 for the same period a year ago.
